name: Ambercorn
summary: Across Mulgore, tauren gather ambercorn beneath ancient trees for the Water of the Seers, a brew used in the Rite of Vision.

sections.title: Gifts of the Canopy
sections.body: Beneath Mulgore’s great trees, ambercorn falls onto the grass for tauren to gather. Tauren see these nuts as bearers of the land’s spiritual vitality and latent magic. Their mystics have understood and used that power for generations. Young hunters and wanderers learn to watch the ground beneath the canopy and honor the Earth Mother’s gifts.

sections.title: The Seer's Brew
sections.body: In Bloodhoof Village, seer Zarlman Two-Moons prepares young tauren for the Rite of Vision with ambercorn. He combines it with stones gathered from the plains’ water wells to make the Water of the Seers. Initiates drink the ceremonial brew before the ancestral flames. Their senses shift, revealing a guiding spirit animal meant to lead them to their next destination.

faq.answer: Ambercorn is a nut that falls from Mulgore’s large, ancient trees. It carries natural magic tied to the spirits of the land.
Ambercorn lies beneath the canopies of Mulgore’s mighty trees, especially around Bloodhoof Village.
Tauren seers combine ambercorn with well stones to brew the Water of the Seers. Initiates drink it during the Rite of Vision, which reveals spiritual guides.

faq.q: Who asks for ambercorn in Bloodhoof Village?
faq.answer: In Bloodhoof Village, seer Zarlman Two-Moons asks initiates to gather ambercorn as part of trials meant to prove their connection to the Earth Mother.

angles.text: As a young tauren, you learn ambercorn is an ingredient in the Rite of the Earth Mother. The brew helps reveal your spiritual path.
As a shaman, you honor natural catalysts like ambercorn. Tauren tradition holds that the Earth Mother places spiritual magic in the harvest of her trees and soil.
